stories.primary_headline: Five killed after car, trying to escape pothole, crashes into state transport bus in Maharashtra's Beed

primary_source.headline: Five killed after car, trying to escape pothole, crashes into state transport bus in Maharashtra's Beed
primary_source.content: Beed: Five people, among them an 11-year-old boy, were killed after their car swerved to avoid potholes and collided with a state transport bus in Maharashtra's Beed district on Sunday morning, police said.The accident occurred around 11 am at Shindewadi Cross Road on the Khamgaon-Pandharpur National Highway in Majalgaon tehsil, around 55 km from the district headquarters, an official said.He said that the victims, all residents of Majalgaon, were travelling towards Tuljapur in neighbouring Dharashiv district when their car crashed into a Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation (MSRTC) bus coming from the opposite direction.The collision reduced the car to a mangled heap of metal, killing all five occupants on the spot, the official said.According to the police, the deceased have been identified as Omkar Mahadev Giri (24), Gajanan Mahadev Namdas (38), his son Samarth (11), Somnath Bade (23), and Anil Acharya (40).Speeding car crash triggers communal, moral and political row in KeralamCCTV footage from the area showed the speeding car lose control while attempting to avoid potholes on a bridge, leading to the head-on crash with the bus, the official said.The fatal crash triggered public anger over the deteriorating condition of roads on the Majalgaon-Telgaon stretch. Locals staged a road blockade alleging that substandard construction and poor maintenance had left fissures and uneven surfaces across the highway, turning the arterial road into an accident zone.Traffic came to a standstill for several hours on the highway due to the protest before senior police and district officials arrived at the scene, pacified the protesters, and restored traffic flow.

stories.primary_headline: Mysuru Dasara airshow: Surya Kiran's dazzling display cut short by rain

primary_source.headline: Mysuru Dasara airshow: Surya Kiran's dazzling display cut short by rain
primary_source.content: Mysuru: The Suryakiran Aerobatic Team (SKAT) of the Indian Air Force, enthralled the jam-packed crowd at Bannimantap ground with their spectacular aerial display during Dasara Airshow in Mysuru on Sunday morning. However, due to rain and inclement weather conditions, the air warriors could only perform three horizontal manoeuvres, including the arrow manoeuvre with nine Hawk Mk 132 aircraft, in the blue sky canvas of Mysuru. The display was complemented by saffron, white and green smoke trails. The team, known for its precision, coordination, synchronisation, discipline and teamwork, performed with all the aircraft operating as a cohesive unit.Mysuru Dasara to feature special tableaux on Army, Navy, Air Force and moreMysuru: Farmers' Dasara turns into platform to inspire community towards independent livelihood, women empowermentThe people who had gathered after the gates of the ground opened at 9 am could witness the show for about 10 minutes from 11.20 am. They were disappointed as the team could not continue the show in view of the safety of pilots and the aircraft due to weather conditions. However, people returned with hope, as the show will be held on Monday too. On Monday, the Surya Kiran team will be flying all the nine aircraft, manufactured under licence by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL). They plan to showcase a series of intricate aerobatic manoeuvres, including both horizontal and vertical ones. Signature manoeuvres such as loops, barrel rolls, inverted flying and the DNA manoeuvres can also be witnessed.Set up in 1996, the Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team has a legacy of representing the Indian Air Force and the nation at air shows and public events across India and abroad. With over 800 displays to its credit, the team is inspiring generations of aviation enthusiasts and young Indians to consider a career in the Indian Air Force.  The display forms part of the team’s continued endeavour to bring the Indian Air Force closer to the people of the country. The show has been an opportunity for people to witness the synergy between man and machine, where every manoeuvre reflects the dedication, skill and teamwork that define the Indian Air Force.

primary_source.headline: Oklahoma Families Faced the Hottest Summer Ever and an Electricity Crisis
primary_source.content: Record heat, a rising demand for power and an electricity crisis are closing in on Oklahoma families trying to keep the lights on and the AC running.
